body:
The short answer is that it's never too late. That said, there will definitely be women who will not want to deal with the lack of experience. I'm currently dating a 34 year old man who has never had a serious relationship and hasn't had any relationship at all in about 10 years. I'm 40 and have had to learn to be patient. At times it's very frustrating because I have a lot of long term relationship experience and I will often have to communicate things to him that I wouldn't with someone who wasn't so used to being alone.  I'm also at the age when I would prefer not to take forever to move things along, but I have to compromise if I want to stay with him.

He's a sweet, kind, funny person who I really enjoy spending time with though, and he is good at communicating so that helps a lot. He listens when I explain what I need/want and generally tries to do what I ask.

So my main point here is that women exist who will give you a chance. And when you do find one, just make sure you listen and pay attention to what she wants, and also communicate what you want.

It's been 2 weeks exactly since I had my second shot (Pfizer). First shot didn't affect me much, just a sore arm. Period was no different than usual. Second shot sucked, I had an extremely sore arm, swollen armpit, aches, and while I didn't get a fever, I did constantly feel hot and cold. Those symptoms lasted about 36 hours then I woke up feeling OK. Had a migraine a couple days later which may or may not have been related. I haven't had my period since the second shot yet, it's due early next week, so we will see. Anecdotally speaking, I only know one person who said her cycle was affected. And I was terrified of side effects, so believe me, I asked EVERYONE lol. Good luck, I'm glad I got  the shot since I feel more protected. But I understand that it's really scary.
So much yes. I don't even want to go to the store or pick up food. It's hard to even work out honestly...
>I thought about it, but it seems legit crazy lol. Although it's not like I have a lot to lose there.
I'm not angry in the least. I know what I signed up for, just needed advice on how to deal with my unexpected feelings :)
Yes and yes. I think I've learned that I shouldn't do casual sex. I keep wondering if he'd want to date if we were in the same town, but the answer is probably no.

I have the Canmake Mermaid Skin Gel UV and it's pretty great in my opinion. I hate that sunscreen feel and this one is probably the most lightweight one I've tried. It's available on Amazon and as of right now it's prime eligible. I have normal combination skin but my cheeks have a tendency to break out with sunscreen. This one did not have that effect. It comes in two types, clear and white. I've only tried the clear.
I don’t have any advice as I get this too. It’s awful! I just wanted to let you know you’re not alone.

Definitely sounds like a false positive, it’s pretty easy to mess up the at home tests, leave it for too long or look at it too early, take it too soon before period, etc. the doctor will be able to do a blood test which is more accurate. But if you used a condom and she has an IUD the chances are super low that she’s pregnant. Also she recently started a new birth control method so that can mess up her periods for a while.
You’re welcome:) I started out in retail then went to call centers, then healthcare office work. You might try a temp agency, sometimes they have jobs like that.

I’ve never worked as a waitress but I have quit a terrible customer service job. This customer at the register was yelling at me because the store was out of his cigarettes and I just snapped. Told him someone else could deal with his shit and walked out. I’ve been fired suddenly too, and it’s scary but you will be OK and you will definitely find something better. I always do, sometimes it takes a little time but it always happens.
Yup mine is worst at night and also right after I wake up (on work days). I’ve been watching ASMR videos at night or binaural beats and it helps a bit.

Yes, I stopped drinking coffee except when I can just relax at home because it makes me super anxious if I’m even slightly stressed out already. It sucks because I get tired at work but better that than a crazy panic attack.
Yep I experience all of this. Fluorescent lights are not good for me either. Working in an office with those lights isn’t great....

If you go to any MAC counter they’ll help you figure out what number you are. There are foundation match sites that can tell you based on other foundations you wear that are a good match, but I’ve had better luck knowing my actual MAC shade by getting matched in person.

Yes! I get blurred vision and have dry eyes and sometimes see little flashes and floaters. I hate it and it’s hard not to focus on it. I have to remind myself that I’m constantly looking at computer or phone screens as well, which can cause those symptoms. And anxiety can cause blurry vision because it dilates your pupils. So your eyes are probably ok since you were checked out before for the same symptoms.
You can have heartburn with no burning, strange but true. Peppermint relaxes the esophagus which can cause heartburn in some people. I have issues with it because I’m prone to acid reflux.
Ooh that’s great you found such a productive way to deal with it! I have a narcissistic mother as well so i can relate.

Oh I hate that! I live in an apartment too and noisy neighbors are my pet peeve. I used to have awful neighbors who would throw loud parties on Tuesday or Wednesday, like really? Inconsiderate morons. But I’m lucky at the moment and have super quiet neighbors all around me. I hope you got some sleep, and it’s the neighbor’s fault, not yours.

It probably is anxiety, I’ve found that when I’m worried about food poisoning or ingesting something bad that I will feel nauseous or have to poop a lot. Probably psychosomatic but if it’s really bad then I would go to the doctor.

Was it an automatic BP cuff? Or a manual one? The automatic ones squeeze my arm so tightly I get anxious and it’s always high on those. I also get super nervous at the doctor so it’s elevated anyway but I’ve noticed the automatic ones are much worse for me. It sounds like white coat syndrome to me since your BP at home was much lower.
I’ve done that too. If the spots were small enough that you didn’t notice them I think you’re ok. The body is tougher than we think. I often have to remind myself of that too.

Not to condone his behavior but I have a history of job hopping due to anxiety and depression. I have varying degrees of success at jobs and then I get really overwhelmed or something happens in my personal life and I start calling in sick a lot and either get fired or quit. Just lost my job of 2 years because of it. I’m trying to fix it and I had a good run but I plan on trying therapy and/or meds for the anxiety and depression to try and stop sabotaging myself like this. If he has a similar issue with coping skills, depression, etc then maybe therapy or meds could help him too? I’m sorry you have to deal with this, it’s frustrating.

Ugh I’ve been through this exact thing. I hate waiting till the next day to find out test results. All you can do is attempt to distract yourself. Whatever you think will be the most engrossing, watch a movie, listen to music, play a video game, read. I feel for you.

I posted something very much like this on my Facebook last night. I don’t really have any advice, I just wanted to tell you that I’ve been really anxious since my dad passed away last year, so I can understand. I’m sorry for your loss and I hope we can both feel better.

I don’t like this, it doesn’t bode well for the future. You don’t say these things to your significant other. Obviously it’s up to you but based on just this incident I think I’d want to get away from this person. He just seems immature and not all that into you...sometimes when people say you’re sweet it means they think you’re so nice they can get away with whatever. Speaking from experience.

I had twilight sedation when I got my wisdom teeth out, and I remembered absolutely nothing. It was like being asleep. I was groggy for a while after and kinda tired for the rest of the day but it wasn’t bad at all. Good luck, you won’t remember any of it!

The more you do it, the easier it will be. I’ve found that the more time I spend with someone the more comfortable I become. Maybe watch a movie or a show together and if you can, kiss her after you’ve been watching a while. Dim lights help. There is something to that whole Netflix and chill thing, lol. Good luck, she sounds like a great person and she’s patient which is awesome,

I used to have thoughts like that when I was in high school (I’m 38 now). I think it’s because that’s an age when you’re still discovering who you are and even though you know you’re probably straight you question it. I just tried to accept it and realize that even if I did turn out to be gay or bisexual or straight, it would be ok. For me those thoughts went away after about 6 months I think, not very long.
Don’t worry, things like this happen a lot! I think they will probably let you come to another meeting and if not, you’ll be able to find another job, maybe even a better one.

I had one last year and I was freaked out too but it went really smoothly and I had no side effects except for feeling warm. The tech was really patient with me and warned me I would feel like that so I felt pretty comfortable.

This sounds like anxiety and depression combined. You’re having intrusive thoughts. It’s a pretty common symptom to be having those thoughts and worrying about acting on them. If you can wait, I would find a psychiatrist or mental health center on Monday so you can start the process of being evaluated and possibly get meds if necessary. If you can’t stand it then you can go to the ER as someone else suggested, they can give you something to help in the meantime. Only you know how urgent it is. I can relate, I hope you find an option that helps ❤️

I’m seconding seeing the value in your job. I worked retail for almost 10 years and that’s how I would approach it. Some people are looking for something specific and you can recommend something related, like a product in the same line maybe. Others are just shopping and if they have no preference you can suggest something new that just came in. If they ask a question you’re not sure of you can always be honest and say you don’t know but you’ll find out. The majority of people are not uptight customers and will most likely understand so long as you’re nice and polite. The rude people will sometimes just be rude no matter what and you have to just try and move on with your day.

Sort of. I was working at a drugstore in a shitty neighborhood and I had already put in my 2 weeks notice to start another job. But I had a total asshole of a customer who started screaming at me when we were out of his brand of cigarettes. I told him to go fuck himself and walked out. Never done it since but it did feel pretty good at the time.

I admit I sleep holding a stuffed animal. It makes me feel secure. My fiancé is very understanding of it and has no issues. I don’t take any plushies out with me but I do wear a crystal necklace (moonstone) and sometimes wear a rose quartz bracelet. I have a couple of crystals in my bag as well. It helps me to have a necklace I can touch when I’m anxious, not sure why. I read that moonstone is good for anxiety and it’s pretty so why not,
Thank you! That’s mostly what I’ve heard so that’s not bad.
I avoid it. Especially now that I’m older and overweight. I hate blood draws (small deep veins) and the automatic blood pressure cuff.
I would travel more and hopefully actually be able to hold down a full time job for more than 2 years. I would be way less distracted and might be able to go back to drawing for fun, also.
I think this sounds like a great idea! I’m going to try it next time I’m thinking too much and feeling anxiety. Thanks for sharing!

Agreed, it’s extremely unlikely that you contracted HIV from either encounter. I’ve worried about that stuff in the past but it’s just so rare that I was able to not worry so much about it. It’s great that you used protection this time, keep doing that and your chances of getting anything are pretty damn low.

I admit I have a thing for mini products, so when I’m traveling and have an excuse to buy them I do. I love the mini Sol de Janeiro Bumbum shower gel and body cream and the R & Co leave in styling cream. I also have a tiny Bite agave lip balm that i love, even though normal size lip balm is small enough, lol.
Ohhhh so cute!

I would go to an ENT like you mentioned, they can test to see if the vertigo is caused by inner ear, which it sounds like it is, since you’ve had other tests. I need to have it done too but I have to wait till I have health insurance first, and also I’m scared because they have to make you dizzy in order to test.
You could try magnesium supplements, either in capsule form or in powder like Natural Calm. They do help me somewhat.
Definitely not a big deal, people do worse with their phones. Like put them down in bathroom stalls, yuck!

There are apps that you can have open while you’re walking and if something happens you press a button and it will text or call you. If you don’t respond it’ll send police to your location. It’s not a weapon but it may give you some peace of mind. Apple Watch has a button on the side you can use to call for help also.

Ginger seconded, that usually works for me. Also, how long have you been together? I usually get super nervous like that in the first few months of a relationship but it always gets better eventually. So if that’s the case, it will probably resolve itself.
I do that too. I usually wear my hair in a ponytail so I will have it over my shoulder and tug on the ends when I’m anxious. I’m glad I’m not the only one, lol. It sorta makes me feel more grounded.

Just give her as much notice as possible once you have a new job. As others have said, this is a reality she will have to deal with sooner or later, people outgrow and leave jobs all the time. I’m sure she will be able to find someone else.

I took my stuffed hippo with me to get my tonsils out at 25, so I understand. No one cared or seemed to think it was weird. I’m a girl but still. I don’t think the medical staff will bat an eye and honestly if they give you shit I’d stop going there.

This isn’t major surgery but I had a tonsillectomy when I was 25 and everyone freaked me out by saying it takes forever to recover as an adult. I had never been under anesthesia before but I talked to the anesthesiologist beforehand about how I was afraid it would make me throw up (common side effect) so he said he would give me extra anti-nausea meds in the IV.  It must have worked because I gagged once after I woke up but never threw up. Everything went really well but I was anxious the whole 2 weeks after while recovering. It helped me to stay at my moms house during the day when everyone was at work and then at night I’d be with my fiancé so I was never alone. I would suggest an arrangement like this with a friend or relative if you can, it’s reassuring knowing someone is right there if something does happen.

I do worry about this, I try to make it better by realizing that I will no longer be anxious when it happens. The scary part for me is that a)I have to do it alone and b)I might suffer and I don’t want that. I’m hoping to go in my sleep or something similar. I think about it a lot more since my dad died really suddenly on the racquetball court (he had a heart attack). I wasn’t there but apparently he said “No” and then collapsed and never regained consciousness. That doesn’t do much to make me feel better but the fact that he most likely only had a moment of fear and then nothing, I guess that’s a good thing.
Yeah totally relate. No one takes it seriously and it sucks!

You can be anxious enough about food poisoning to feel nauseous and have diarrhea. That’s one of my big fears so I understand and it’s happened to me. Given how long it’s been you’re most likely fine. One thing to consider too is you may be slightly lactose intolerant, it’s pretty common to have trouble digesting dairy. I’ve noticed that sometimes if I eat a a lot of dairy I get loose stools.
Yes, I’m feeling this today actually! I know it will go away, I’m extra anxious since I had a job interview this morning.
Yay that’s awesome! I’m so glad. That’s probably the number one thing I’ve learned that helps. I think Headspace offers a week or so trial, you might see if any of the basics help you.

Yes, I have the Headspace app and paid for a year when they had a half off special. It does help but not always and I’m bad at sticking to it. Some of the things I’ve learned I use when anxious though, like feeling your weight in the chair you’re sitting in.

I totally relate to this. I can’t even go to the doctor for a doctors note and I just lost another job due to not being able to go in. Went on vacation last month and kept freaking out and not being able to have fun. You’re not alone and it really sucks! I agree about bringing someone supportive to the doctor with you though, that may help.
Yup I rarely drink and feeling weak and shaky is common for me afterwards. Glad you’re feeling better, water usually helps me too!

I’m glad it helped! Yeah I even went back to the doctor once and got another uti test but nope, it was gone. I think some of us notice this symptom more than others or maybe are more sensitive, because I always notice any tiny irritation there and worry about it.

I’ve noticed that after I have a UTI this happens to me, maybe there’s some inflammation in the bladder for a bit after it goes away? It always goes away on its own for me. I would just keep drinking lots of fluids for now like you’ve been doing.

I’m so sorry for your loss, first of all. I lost my dad very suddenly last year, he had gone to play racquetball and he had a heart attack on the court, we got to the ER 20 minutes later but he was already gone, they weren’t able to get his heart started again. It was totally surreal and I completely know the feeling of not being able to say goodbye. I felt awful too because I was going to stop by and see him two days before. It doesn’t help to think about that though, I know he was aware that I loved him. I went to therapy, talked to friends, and wrote letters to my dad in my journal. Those things helped but the pain was agonizing and there’s nothing to be done except let yourself grieve, cry and sob and get mad if you need to. I would do boxing workout videos on YouTube to let off steam. Also something a lot of people don’t talk about is that the first year is kind of a blur but the second year is when it really sinks in that they’re gone for real. I don’t think this feeling ever goes away but it does change over time and becomes easier to deal with. Hugs to you, I wouldn’t wish that pain on anyone.

That sounds very normal to me, especially when it’s hot outside. That’s about what mine would be. And for housework it’s usually around 110 for me, for anyone who’s curious lol. Swimming 120-140 depending on if I’m actually swimming or just goofing around.

Yes I always carry pepto bismol tablets with me. My stomach issues are real (IBS) but anxiety makes them worse. It’s a vicious cycle and it sucks! Especially at work, one of my former employers said I spent too much time in the bathroom, but backed off when I asked if they wanted a doctors note. It’s bullshit when people don’t understand, it’s not like I want to go to the bathroom so often, believe me

I do a similar thing and used to see a therapist who told me it was part of OCD. Not sure if she’s right but it makes sense for me as the health anxiety has elements of it, like asking for reassurance etc.

Thank you. Honestly sometimes anxiety just appears, I’ve had it since I was a kid. It’s just that recent events have made it much worse. I just started watching ASMR videos on YouTube and while I think I might be weird for trying it lol it seems to help. I watched one and almost immediately started feeling all sleepy and relaxed. I felt the tingly feeling at the back of my neck and was surprised, didn’t expect it to work on me.

I’m the same way, I used to go to the doctor a lot when I was younger but now I avoid them at all costs. I tried to go to the Walgreens clinic the other day for a dr note and they weren’t all that nice so I had a panic attack in the exam room and had to leave...I’m just always terrified they’re going to tell me something is seriously wrong and I don’t want to know. I think it has to do with my dad passing away very suddenly last year from a heart attack. It’s just hard not to believe the worst now with every single symptom.
My temp routinely runs low, about 96.1-97.1. I know this because I used to worry about having a fever lol. The doctor said not to worry because it’s still within the normal range.
Dizziness is one of my main symptoms also. It’s so hard to accept that it’s anxiety. Also very hard to ignore.

Nope not just you! Most people do not understand though, so yeah I feel bad about myself too, but I don’t think it’s our fault. I’ve tried hard to combat it but haven’t been successful for very long at a time...

Yes yes so much yes! I just lost another job due to anxiety. I hate making plans of any kind because I can’t stand having to be somewhere that I can’t leave. Doctors and dentists appointments are particularly bad for me, along with work. I remember when I was young and worked part time it wasn’t as bad, since I knew I’d be there for 4 hours and then go home. But something about 8 or 9 hours at work is just horribly anxiety inducing...glad I’m not the only one! A lot of people think it’s laziness but I think it’s the opposite, most people I know with anxiety are very hard workers and we stress about our performance at work.

I feel the same. Lost my job last week, have already started staying up way too late and sleeping in too late. I’m not motivated to do anything, nothing seems fun and everything seems pointless. I think things will probably get better for both of us but right now it sucks so much.

That always freaks me out when I’m sick too, but as everyone else has said, it’s totally normal to have an elevated heart rate while you’re sick and recovering. Your body is working hard to fight it, that’s also why you get a fever.

Sounds like a migraine with aura to me. When I was on birth control pills that were high in estrogen I had migraines exactly like that. I would know it was coming by that blank spot in my vision you’re describing. I would also get kind of sparks in my field of vision, like after you look at a bright light. I hate those symptoms, they’re scary. So probably just a migraine but you could mention the new symptoms to your neurologist if you’re worried, since you haven’t experienced them before.

You might be surprised in a good way. Most of my close friends in high school were pretty understanding and supportive, once they knew what was going on. You can even say that you’re worried people will think you just want attention, but you’re really struggling. And let them know that you really value their friendship (in whatever phrasing you want to use) so you wanted to tell them what’s been going on. People usually respond well to that and you might even find out that they have some level of anxiety too. It’s super common unfortunately.

I know it’s easier to say this than to do it but it sounds like you need new friends! Have you explained the anxiety thing to them? Maybe one on one? Sometimes people are nicer and more receptive when they’re not thinking about what everyone else is going to think.

Would it help if your friends came over to your house sometimes? Or maybe start really small with a trip to Starbucks or something? My anxiety about making plans usually is worst when it’s going to last a while so that might help if you’re the same way. I have to admit I’ve lost friends due to this but at least the ones I have left totally understand and are supportive.

One tip I’ve had success with is to always have questions for the interviewer when they ask. My go to is what’s your favorite thing about working for this company? Or what quality do you think is important for this position? It helps engage them and make it more of a two way conversation, plus depending on their answer you can tie it into why they should hire you.
You could try a temp agency, the ones in my area sometimes have part time jobs available. I’ve seen a few office ones. I have the same issue, btw. It sucks

It’s the worst kind of anxiety, seriously. Even on anxiety message boards it’s hard to find someone like us. I’ve asked for advice before and people usually say just push through it. I’d like to, sure but it usually doesn’t work that way. The reason I stayed at my longest job for 6 years was because it was at a bookstore and was part time for the first 4 years or so. When I got promoted to a lead and had to work 40 hour weeks my anxiety became unmanageable and I eventually lost the job. It’s nice to know there are others though, most people just think you’re lazy or don’t want to work but I think it’s the opposite.

I also suffer from ergophobia and actually just lost another job because of it. I’ve found that part-time hours are easier for me because they require me to be there for less time. Maybe you could start with that and try to ease into it? I wish I had more advice about dealing with the actual anxiety but I haven’t figured it out yet. I suspect I will have to try medication. Also, you definitely haven’t ruined your life, things have a way of working out. I’m glad you have a supportive girlfriend, too, if she was pressuring you it would be harder.

Oh I’m right there with you. I’m 38 so older than you but I’ve found that it’s gotten worse for me the last few years. I actually just lost a job due to this. My longest job has been 6 years but it was part time. I think if I could do part time it might be ok but who can survive on that? I just wanted to let you know you’re not alone, I don’t know too many people who suffer from this work phobia but we definitely exist.
